items.abstract: <jats:p>Model merging combines knowledge from multiple pretrained models into a single unified model without full retraining, offering an alternative to extending multilingual neural machine translation (MNMT) via con&#x2;tinued pretraining or fine-tuning when new languages or additional data become available. Heterogeneous encoder–tokenizer pairs, however, break naive merging: incompatible tokenizers produce non-isomorphic token sequences (tokenization bias), and independent pretraining yields mismatched hidden-state bases and depth-wise scale distributions (representation bias), inducing negative parameter interference. HyUOTMerge addresses both mismatches through a geometry-aware framework. Stage 1, Fréchet-Centered Hyperbolic Normalization (FCHN), reduces representation bias via Stiefel-constrained projection to a shared dimension, Klein lifting with soft-logarithm tempering, depth-wise Fréchet centering, and tangent-space scaling, yielding supports on a depth–hyperbolic product space. Stage 2, Unbalanced Optimal-Transport Fusion (UOT-Fuse), reduces tokenization bias by aligning these supports through a bias-corrected unbalanced Sinkhorn diver&#x2;gence under a depth-aware hyperbolic ground cost with tangent-space barycentric projection, enabling partial matchability without enforcing unreliable cross-view correspondences; the unified encoder inherits the ref&#x2;erence tokenization as a tokenizer-agnostic feature extractor for MNMT decoders. On 13 Indic→English directions trained on 9M parallel pairs and evaluated on IN22-Conv/Gen, HyUOTMerge yields consistent improvements; on IN22-Conv, macro-average BLEU increases from 37.95 (IndicTrans2) to 39.23–41.38 across three heterogeneous pairings (M1–M3), with a maximum gain of +9.28 BLEU on Kannada, while outperform&#x2;ing NLLB-200 on 10 of 11 directions where it is available and substantially exceeding LLaMA-2-13B-LoRA and NLIP baselines. These results support, to the best of the authors’ knowledge, the first heterogeneous encoder merging approach that addresses tokenization-induced sequence mismatch and pretraining-induced representation mismatch within a single merging objective.</jats:p>
title: HyUOTMerge: Unbalanced Optimal-Transport Fusion for Heterogeneous Encoder Merging for Indic Multilingual Translation

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
               <jats:p>We introduce and study a simple model capturing the main features of unbalanced optimal transport. It is based on equipping the conical extension of the group of all diffeomorphisms with a natural metric, which allows a Riemannian submersion to the space of volume forms of arbitrary total mass. We describe its finite-dimensional version and present a concise comparison study of the geometry, Hamiltonian features, and geodesics for this and other extensions. One of the corollaries of this approach is that along any geodesic the total mass evolves with constant acceleration, as an object’s height in a constant buoyancy field.</jats:p>
title: Simple Unbalanced Optimal Transport
